q: What is the Architect's monthly fee at the HIGH end (6%) of the RPF range?
scenario: A larger mixed-use commercial building generates a gross monthly rental income of PHP 3,000,000.00. The Owner engages the Architect as Consulting Architect for post-construction services only, compensated by value-pricing under Sec. 10.2.1 at the RPF of 4% to 6% of gross rental under Sec. 10.3.

q: An Owner wants the same Architect who designed and supervised the project to also continue managing the completed building on an ongoing basis. Which Sec. 10.1 arrangement fits this situation?
o: Consulting Architect for post-construction services only
Dual capacity as Architect-of-Record and Consulting Architect for post-construction services
n: Because the Owner wants the original Architect-of-Record to also take on ongoing post-construction/building-management duties, this is the dual-capacity arrangement under Sec. 10.1.1. (Source: SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.1.1)

q: If the building sustains this PHP 3,000,000.00 monthly rental for a full year, what would be the Architect's fee at the MIDPOINT rate of 5% applied to the annual gross rental?
n: Annual gross rental = PHP 3,000,000.00 x 12 = PHP 36,000,000.00. At the midpoint rate of 5% (halfway between the 4% and 6% RPF bounds): 5% x PHP 36,000,000.00 = PHP 1,800,000.00. (Source: SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.3)
scenario: A larger mixed-use commercial building generates a gross monthly rental income of PHP 3,000,000.00. The Owner engages the Architect as Consulting Architect for post-construction services only, compensated by value-pricing under Sec. 10.2.1 at the RPF of 4% to 6% of gross rental under Sec. 10.3.

q: An Owner wants the building administrator's fee to rise and fall with the building's actual rental income, to motivate efficient operations. Which Sec. 10.2 compensation method should the parties adopt?
o: Value-pricing or percentage of gross rentals, maintenance and security fees
n: Value-pricing (Sec. 10.2.1), recommended at 4%-6% of gross rental, ties the Architect's compensation to the building's rental performance and is explicitly described as incentive-based. (Source: SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.2.1; Sec. 10.3)

q: Which of the following BEST describes the scope of Sec. 10 (Post-Construction Services, SPP Doc. 205), as distinguished from adjacent SPP sections such as Sec. 9 (Construction Management) and Sec. 11 (Comprehensive Architectural Services)?
o: It governs the Architect's services rendered to the Owner AFTER project completion, as Building Administrator and/or Property Manager, compensated chiefly through value-pricing on gross rentals
It governs the Architect's supervision of contractors and construction cost control during the construction phase
It governs the Architect's role in assembling a full project team of engineers, market analysts, and lawyers as Project Manager
It governs Design-Build Services where the Architect is also the project's contractor
n: Sec. 10 specifically covers services AFTER the building is completed and occupied — building administration/property management — distinct from Sec. 9's construction-phase management and Sec. 11's comprehensive project-management/team-assembly role (both of which are separate SPP topics). (Source: SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10 (overall scope); cf. Sec. 9, Sec. 11)

q: A property developer wants to keep an Architect on standby for periodic post-construction advice throughout the year, paying a base amount plus reimbursement for expenses actually incurred. Which Sec. 10.2 method matches this?
o: Value-pricing or percentage of gross rentals
n: Sec. 10.2.4, Retainer plus Reimbursable Expenses, is the method suited to a standing/standby engagement where a base retainer is paid together with reimbursement of expenses incurred. (Source: SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.2.4)

q: In Post-Construction Services, the Architect performing these services may also be referred to by which title(s)?
n: Sec. 10.2 describes the Architect performing Post-Construction Services as one 'engaged as the Building Administrator and/or Property Manager.' (Source: SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.2)

q: Using the LOW end of the RPF range (4%), what is the Architect's monthly post-construction management fee?
scenario: An Architect is engaged as Building Administrator/Property Manager for a newly turned-over commercial building. The building generates a gross monthly rental income of PHP 1,500,000.00. The Owner and Architect agree to compensate the Architect using value-pricing under Sec. 10.2.1, applying the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) of 4% to 6% of gross rental under Sec. 10.3.

q: Aside from the dual-capacity arrangement, what is the second manner by which an Architect may provide post-construction services under Sec. 10.1?
o: As Project Manager for the entire project
As Consulting Architect for post-construction services only
n: Sec. 10.1.2 provides that the Architect may instead work purely as Consulting Architect for post-construction services only — i.e., without necessarily having been the project's Architect-of-Record. (Source: SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.1.2)

q: What is the full monthly fee range (low to high) that the Architect may charge under Sec. 10.3's value-pricing RPF?
n: At 4% and 6% of PHP 1,500,000.00, the range is PHP 60,000.00 (4%) to PHP 90,000.00 (6%). (Source: SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.3)
scenario: An Architect is engaged as Building Administrator/Property Manager for a newly turned-over commercial building. The building generates a gross monthly rental income of PHP 1,500,000.00. The Owner and Architect agree to compensate the Architect using value-pricing under Sec. 10.2.1, applying the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) of 4% to 6% of gross rental under Sec. 10.3.

q: The first-listed method of compensation under Sec. 10.2, 'value-pricing,' bases the Architect's fee on a percentage of what?
o: The Owner's net annual profit after taxes
The Architect's regular design fee under SPP Doc. 202
Gross rentals, maintenance and security fees
n: Sec. 10.2.1 defines value-pricing as compensation based on a percentage of gross rentals, maintenance fees, and security fees generated by the completed building. (Source: SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.2.1)

q: What is the Architect's monthly fee at the LOW end (4%) of the RPF range?
scenario: A larger mixed-use commercial building generates a gross monthly rental income of PHP 3,000,000.00. The Owner engages the Architect as Consulting Architect for post-construction services only, compensated by value-pricing under Sec. 10.2.1 at the RPF of 4% to 6% of gross rental under Sec. 10.3.

q: Sec. 10.3 describes the 4%-6% value-pricing fee as an 'incentive-type' management fee. What is this incentive structure intended to achieve?
o: A fixed income for the Architect regardless of building performance
More efficient and economical building operation while maximizing building revenues
Reduction of the Architect's liability insurance premiums
Faster completion of the original construction schedule
n: Sec. 10.3 states that this incentive-type management fee 'will ensure more efficient and economical operation and maximize building revenues,' aligning the Architect's compensation with the building's rental performance. (Source: SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.3)

q: How much MORE would the Architect earn per month at the 6% rate compared to the 4% rate?
n: PHP 180,000.00 (6%) minus PHP 120,000.00 (4%) = PHP 60,000.00, which equals 2% of the PHP 3,000,000.00 gross monthly rental. (Source: SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.3)
scenario: A larger mixed-use commercial building generates a gross monthly rental income of PHP 3,000,000.00. The Owner engages the Architect as Consulting Architect for post-construction services only, compensated by value-pricing under Sec. 10.2.1 at the RPF of 4% to 6% of gross rental under Sec. 10.3.

q: A commercial building's Owner already has a separate Architect-of-Record on file, but now wants to hire a different Architect purely to consult on post-construction building administration matters. Which Sec. 10.1 manner applies?
o: Consulting Architect for post-construction services only
Project Manager under Comprehensive Architectural Services
Dual capacity as Architect-of-Record and Consulting Architect
n: Since a different Architect is engaged solely for post-construction consultation, without assuming the Architect-of-Record role, this falls under Sec. 10.1.2 — Consulting Architect for post-construction services only. (Source: SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.1.2)

q: What is the Architect's monthly post-construction management fee at this agreed 5% rate?
n: 5% x PHP 2,000,000.00 = PHP 100,000.00, which falls within the 4%-6% RPF range set by Sec. 10.3. (Source: SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.3)
scenario: A boutique office building has a gross monthly rental income of PHP 2,000,000.00. The Owner and Architect settle on a value-pricing rate of exactly 5% under Sec. 10.3.

q: An Owner prefers to pay the Architect-Administrator a fixed amount every month, independent of how much rental income the building earns. Which Sec. 10.2 method describes this arrangement?
o: Value-pricing or percentage of gross rentals
n: Sec. 10.2.2 lists 'Monthly salary/fee' as a compensation method — a fixed periodic amount unrelated to the building's rental performance, unlike value-pricing. (Source: SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.2.2)

q: Under the Schedule of Professional Practice (SPP), which document number and section govern Post-Construction Services?
n: Post-Construction Services are governed by SPP Document 205, taken up as Sec. 10 of the compiled SPP. (Source: SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10 (title))

q: A Consulting Architect wants to bill the Owner strictly according to the actual hours and payroll cost of the personnel assigned to a post-construction assignment, multiplied by a standard factor for overhead and profit. Which Sec. 10.2 method is this?
o: Value-pricing or percentage of gross rentals
n: Sec. 10.2.3, Multiple of Direct Personnel Expense, compensates the Architect based on personnel costs multiplied by an agreed factor. (Source: SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.2.3)

q: Under Sec. 10.1, one of the two ways an Architect may contract with the Owner for post-construction services is to work in a dual capacity. What does this dual capacity consist of?
o: Project Manager and Consulting Architect for design-build services
Architect-of-Record and Consulting Architect for post-construction services
Consulting Architect and Full-Time Supervisor simultaneously
n: Sec. 10.1.1 allows the Architect to work in a dual capacity as Architect-of-Record (AoR) AND as Consulting Architect for post-construction services. (Source: SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.1.1)

q: Using the HIGH end of the RPF range (6%), what is the Architect's monthly post-construction management fee?
scenario: An Architect is engaged as Building Administrator/Property Manager for a newly turned-over commercial building. The building generates a gross monthly rental income of PHP 1,500,000.00. The Owner and Architect agree to compensate the Architect using value-pricing under Sec. 10.2.1, applying the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) of 4% to 6% of gross rental under Sec. 10.3.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the methods of compensation listed under Sec. 10.2 for Post-Construction Services?
o: Value-pricing or percentage of gross rentals, maintenance and security fees
n: 'Percentage of Construction Cost Project' is a Construction Management Services (Sec. 9.2.1.1) compensation method, not one of the five listed for Post-Construction Services under Sec. 10.2 (value-pricing/percentage of gross rentals, monthly salary/fee, multiple of DPE, retainer plus reimbursable expenses, and professional fee plus expenses). (Source: SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.2; cf. Sec. 9.2.1.1)

q: If the PHP 1,500,000.00 monthly rental holds steady all year, what would be the Architect's ANNUAL fee range (4% to 6%) based on the annualized gross rental?
n: Annual gross rental = PHP 1,500,000.00 x 12 = PHP 18,000,000.00. At 4%: PHP 720,000.00; at 6%: PHP 1,080,000.00. (Source: SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.3)
scenario: An Architect is engaged as Building Administrator/Property Manager for a newly turned-over commercial building. The building generates a gross monthly rental income of PHP 1,500,000.00. The Owner and Architect agree to compensate the Architect using value-pricing under Sec. 10.2.1, applying the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) of 4% to 6% of gross rental under Sec. 10.3.

q: Per Sec. 10.3, what is the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) range based on value-pricing for Post-Construction Services?
o: 1.5% to 3% of the Project Construction Cost
2% to 5% of the Project Construction Cost
1% to 1.5% of the Project Construction Cost
n: Sec. 10.3 sets the RPF based on value-pricing at 4% to 6% of gross rental (the 1%-1.5% and 1.5%-3% PCC-based rates belong instead to Full-Time Supervision and Construction Management Services, respectively). (Source: SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.3)
